10 Best Weekend Getaways in the USA | My Favorite Destinations

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by

Instaread

These are my 10 absolute favorite weekend getaways in the USA. Destinations I find myself returning to again and again because they're easy to get to, offer plenty to see and do, and can be explored in just two or three days.

Between full-time jobs, school schedules, and other commitments, finding time to travel isn't always easy. Sometimes, a quick weekend getaway is all you can fit into your calendar.

Weekend getaways have become a staple for Jake and me. After years of squeezing in Friday-to-Sunday trips, we've found a handful of destinations that keep us coming back.

These are my picks for the best weekend getaways in the USA because they're easy to get to, have plenty to offer in just a few days, and are worth visiting more than once.

Whether you're looking for great food, culture, outdoor adventures, wineries, or shopping, there's something on this list for you.

Final Thoughts on the Best Weekend Getaways in the USA

Let’s take a look at the BEST weekend getaways in the USA

1. Scottsdale, Arizona

One of the best weekend getaways in the USA for relaxation and desert views

Scottsdale is hands down one of my (and Jake's) favorite weekend getaways in the USA. We visit once or twice a year and always leave wishing we could stay longer.

There's just something about the laid-back atmosphere, gorgeous desert landscape, morning hikes, and friendly people that keeps us coming back.

Another reason I love Scottsdale is how convenient everything is. Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport (PHX) is just a 20-minute drive from Scottsdale, depending on where you're staying. Most of the best restaurants, shopping, hiking trails, and resorts are within a short drive of one another.

Scottsdale really is a beautiful destination. The landscaping is pristine, with colorful desert flowers, towering cacti, and mountain views in almost every direction.

The coffee shop and restaurant scene is on point, and there are desert hikes for just about every fitness level. The resorts offer gorgeous pools for lounging, plus spas that put you in ultimate relaxation mode.

Where to Stay and What to Do in Scottsdale

Stay at the Omni Montelucia or Andaz Scottsdale, my two favorite resorts.

For coffee, don't miss Berdena's and Schmooze, two of my favorite Scottsdale coffee shops. When it comes to restaurants, Virtù Honest Craft, Lon's at Hermosa Inn, Diego Pops, Olive & Ivy, and The Mission are all worth a visit.

And if you enjoy a good cocktail, a visit to Century Grand PHX is an absolute must. It's hands down one of my favorite cocktail experiences on the planet.

This innovative, immersive concept features three themed bars inspired by the turn of the century: a nautical tiki/pirate ship, a Pullman-style train car, and a New Orleans-inspired apothecary. Each is completely different and worth experiencing.

HAVE EXTRA TIME IN SCOTTSDALE?

Drive about two hours north and spend a night or two in Sedona. Known for its stunning red rock formations, hiking trails, and spiritual vortex sites, Sedona is a wonderful place to slow down, relax, and spend time in nature.

The hikes are breathtaking, with enough trails to keep you coming back for years. On our most recent visit, we tackled Devil's Bridge and Cathedral Rock, two of Sedona's most popular hikes.

Unlike Scottsdale, Sedona has four distinct seasons and is noticeably cooler because of its higher elevation.

Sedona also has a charming downtown area, although traffic and crowds can be an issue on holiday weekends.

I was pleasantly surprised by the restaurant scene, especially the prices. Given Sedona's popularity, I expected everything to be extremely overpriced, but found many restaurants comparable to what we'd pay in Dallas. Elote Cafe and Mariposa were our two favorites.

We stayed at the Inn Above Oak Creek, a lovely spot near the heart of Sedona.

If you're looking to splurge, check out L'Auberge de Sedona, conveniently located near downtown, or Enchantment Resort, tucked among the red rocks of Boynton Canyon and closer to some of the area's most scenic trails.

2. Charleston, South Carolina

The best US weekend getaway for Southern charm and comfort food

I head to Charleston when I'm in the mood for great food, history, culture, and a little Southern charm, all at a slower pace. The city has welcomed some spectacular new hotels in recent years, and the restaurant scene alone will have you booking your next trip before you've even left.

Charleston is the perfect city to explore at your own pace, with its picturesque streets, waterfront views, colorful historic homes, and beautiful architecture.

Whenever I visit, I try to book a hotel that offers complimentary bikes. Cycling around Charleston is one of my favorite things to do. Traffic is generally manageable, and it's easy to stick to the quieter side streets and residential neighborhoods.

A historic walking tour is a must. If you're looking to splurge, book a private sailboat cruise around Charleston Harbor. And for something a little different, join the Pleasing Terrors Ghost Walking Tour.

When it comes to dining, you really can't go wrong. Book dinner at The Ordinary, FIG, Vern's, or The Grocery. Don't miss brunch at Husk, and if you're visiting on a Saturday, make time for the farmers market in Marion Square.

One thing I encourage visitors to skip is the horse-drawn carriage rides, particularly when horses are pulling large groups of people in Charleston's intense heat and humidity. Instead, get some exercise and explore the city on foot or by bike!

The same goes for New Orleans. If you choose to participate in a carriage ride or any activity involving animals, please do your research and support companies that follow animal welfare regulations and prioritize the well-being of their animals. Responsible operators do exist, but it's up to us as travelers to seek them out and support them.

3. Napa Valley or Sonoma/Healdsburg

The best US weekend getaway for wine lovers and a romantic escape

With three major airports to choose from—Oakland, San Francisco, and Sacramento—finding a good flight deal or schedule is usually pretty easy. If you're heading to Healdsburg or Sonoma County, Santa Rosa's Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (STS) is another convenient option, with the added bonus of a much shorter drive to Healdsburg.

Napa Valley is one of my favorite weekend getaways in the USA for wine lovers. You could easily spend your entire trip wine tasting, but there's plenty more to enjoy beyond the vineyards.

Jake and I typically book one to three wine tastings a day, leaving plenty of time to explore the charming towns throughout the valley. Strolling through Yountville is always a must, along with a stop at Oxbow Public Market in downtown Napa.

If Napa Valley feels a little too crowded or touristy for your taste, consider Sonoma or Healdsburg instead. Both offer a more laid-back atmosphere, excellent wineries, and a slightly more local feel.

Napa Valley is an ideal destination for a long weekend, although I recommend staying at least three nights. Between the flight and the hour-plus drive from the airport, we find that an extra night makes the trip much more worthwhile.

4. Willamette Valley, Oregon – My Hometown!

The perfect weekend getaway for wine and nature—without the California prices

Napa (well, let's be honest, California in general) has gotten VERY expensive. If you're looking for a wine country getaway that's easier on the budget, more laid-back, and less crowded, head to the Willamette Valley, the heart of Oregon Wine Country.

The Willamette Valley is especially known for its world-class Pinot Noir, with plenty of smaller, family-owned wineries offering a more personal and intimate tasting experience than you'll typically find in Napa.

Base yourself in McMinnville, my hometown! One of my favorite hotels is the Atticus Hotel, a beautiful boutique property within walking distance of some of my favorite restaurants and shops in downtown Mac (as the locals call it).

For something a little more secluded, Youngberg Hill is a nice bed and breakfast tucked into the rolling hills of a working winery. Another favorite is A'Tuscan Estate, a charming little bed and breakfast just steps from downtown McMinnville. It's a hidden gem that not many visitors know about.

Spend your days sipping Oregon Pinot Noir, taking in the beautiful vineyard views, and treating yourself to a spa appointment at The Allison Inn & Spa.

Have extra time in the Willamette Valley?

Consider adding a night or two in Pacific City along the Oregon Coast. It's a beautiful change of scenery and one of my favorite places to enjoy Oregon's rugged coastline.

A stay at Headlands Coastal Lodge & Spa is especially memorable, with views of Haystack Rock, fireplaces in every room, and s'mores around a beach bonfire.

The hotel is also great at helping guests arrange activities, including kayaking on the Nestucca River, guided hikes, and other outdoor adventures.

There are some fantastic coastal hikes in the area, including Cape Lookout, where you'll find sweeping views of the Pacific Ocean.

5. Santa Barbara, California

A weekend getaway that offers a little bit of everything—nature, beaches, food, wine, and great weather

Santa Barbara had been on my radar for years. When I finally found a good flight deal and made my way there, I was beyond impressed. It's one of those destinations that really does seem to have it all.

Downtown Santa Barbara is incredibly walkable, a huge perk, especially if you plan to explore the Urban Wine Trail. A stretch of State Street, the main downtown thoroughfare, has also been pedestrianized, making it even more enjoyable to wander between shops, restaurants, and tasting rooms.

The coffee shop scene alone made me want to move to Santa Barbara, and the restaurants exceeded my expectations.

Add in gorgeous ocean views, hiking trails, and the nearby wine regions of Los Olivos and Santa Ynez, and you've got a destination that offers a little bit of everything.

On our first visit, I managed to snag a deal at the Ritz-Carlton Bacara in neighboring Goleta. While I loved the property, we decided to stay downtown on our second visit and much preferred having restaurants, coffee shops, and shopping right outside our hotel door. For a weekend getaway, the convenience of being able to walk everywhere is hard to beat.

We stayed at Hotel Virginia Santa Barbara, Tapestry Collection by Hilton. I found a great rate, so it worked well for our trip, but I wouldn't necessarily recommend it otherwise. The hotel was fine, but the overall finishes and construction felt a bit cheap. I'd look at other downtown options before booking it again.

Jake and I stopped by the Hotel Californian for drinks, and I immediately wanted to book a stay. It's a fantastic option if you're looking to splurge, as is the ultra-bougie Rosewood Miramar Beach in nearby Montecito.

Another thing I love about Santa Barbara is the casual Southern California vibe. Dress up or dress down, it really doesn't matter (well, unless you're at the Rosewood).

The only real downside? Santa Barbara hotels don't come cheap. Either put some serious effort into finding a good hotel deal or go into your trip knowing you'll be paying a pretty penny for your stay.

That said, between the food, wine, beaches, and beautiful weather, Santa Barbara is absolutely worth a spot on this list of the best weekend getaways in the USA.

6. New York City, New York

One of the best weekend getaways in the USA for shopping, dining, and city lovers

Whether you're planning a girls' shopping trip, looking to try some incredible restaurants, check out the rooftop bar and nightlife scene, or catch a Broadway show or two, New York City has something for everyone. There's enough to keep you busy whether it's your first visit or your 20th.

Embrace your inner tourist and visit Times Square and Central Park, or spend your days wandering some of my favorite neighborhoods, including SoHo, the West Village, and the Upper East Side. I personally prefer exploring the smaller neighborhood streets, popping into boutiques, and discovering new coffee shops and restaurants along the way.

Looking for a fun atmosphere with great food? Buddakan, TAO Downtown, and Beauty & Essex are all worth checking out, especially if you're in the mood for a lively night out.

For Italian, L'Artusi in the West Village is one of my favorites. After dinner, head to Mr. Purple or The Crown for rooftop drinks and beautiful views of the NYC skyline.

7. Chicago, Illinois

A great NYC alternative for city lovers who want something more manageable for a quick weekend

Chicago in the summer is glorious. Early fall, when the weather is still pleasant but the crowds have started to thin, is a close second.

The moment the weather warms up, Chicago comes alive with rooftop bars, outdoor patios, and people enjoying the sunshine. And like any major city, the restaurant scene is fantastic.

Shop till you drop along the Magnificent Mile, enjoy amazing Mediterranean cuisine at Aba, and don't miss dinner at Bavette's Bar & Boeuf, one of my favorites. For cocktails, check out the tiki-inspired Three Dots and a Dash.

One of the best things to do in Chicago is the architecture river cruise. It's a fantastic way to appreciate the city's impressive architecture while learning a bit about its history.

Other favorites include catching a concert at Millennium Park, seeing a Broadway musical, and, of course, making the obligatory stop at Cloud Gate (better known as the Bean).

For a major city, Chicago feels surprisingly manageable for a quick weekend getaway. Downtown is walkable, public transportation is convenient, and you can fit quite a bit into two or three days without feeling like you're constantly rushing from one attraction to the next.

One tip: If flight prices and schedules are comparable, I prefer flying into Midway Airport over O'Hare. Midway is smaller, easier to navigate, and typically takes around 25–35 minutes to reach downtown by train.

O'Hare is a much larger airport, and getting downtown generally takes longer, especially if you're driving during rush hour. That said, the Blue Line makes getting into the city relatively easy from O'Hare as well.

8. La Jolla and San Diego, California

One of the best weekend getaways in the USA for coastal vibes and great weather year-round

With its mild temperatures and sunny Southern California weather, La Jolla is a great weekend getaway just about any time of year. Spend your days outdoors enjoying ocean views, scenic hikes, and leisurely brunches on restaurant patios.

One of the things I love about this area is how easy it is to explore several beach towns in one trip. Head about 20–30 minutes south from La Jolla and you're in downtown San Diego. Drive about 20 minutes north and you'll reach the beach town of Del Mar.

Hike the trails at Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve, enjoy Italian cuisine on the rooftop at Catania, watch the sunset over the Pacific, and visit La Jolla Cove to see the local sea lions. Add in a long walk along Del Mar's beach, and you've got yourself a pretty perfect weekend getaway.

My favorite place to stay in La Jolla Village is The Orli. It's within walking distance of everything—shops, coffee shops, restaurants, and scenic walks along the water. It's a tiny boutique hotel that was a bit of an under-the-radar find until Travel + Leisure recently featured it, so I'd recommend booking in advance.

La Valencia is a good backup option with a nice pool, though it has a more traditional feel compared to The Orli's newer, modern style.

If you're looking for more of a romantic resort getaway, the Fairmont Grand Del Mar is a luxury resort tucked into the hills near Del Mar.

Another perk is the convenience of San Diego International Airport (SAN). Located just minutes from downtown San Diego, it makes it easy to spend some time exploring the city on your way to or from La Jolla.

9. Orlando, Florida – Disney World & Universal Studios

The best US weekend getaway for families and bringing out your inner child

We all need a weekend here and there where we can forget about our responsibilities and bring out our inner child.

Jake surprised me with a trip to The Wizarding World of Harry Potter at Universal Orlando for our first anniversary, and I couldn't have been happier! Yes, I'm a total Harry Potter nerd.

Orlando is a great choice for a long weekend getaway, though I'd recommend at least two nights to make the trip worthwhile.

We typically fly in early Saturday morning and spend the afternoon relaxing by the hotel pool. If there's a special event at one of the parks that evening, like Halloween Horror Nights at Universal, we'll do that on our first night. Sunday is usually a full park day, and Monday we'll squeeze in another park before catching the latest flight home.

My biggest tip is to decide which parks you want to visit before booking your hotel. With limited time, you'll want to stay as close to the parks as possible.

If you're visiting Universal, look for deals at one of the on-site hotels. Several are within walking distance of the parks, while others offer convenient water taxi transportation.

I've stayed at Universal's Loews Sapphire Falls Resort twice now and especially love the walk along the waterway to Universal Studios. Staying here also gets you early park admission, which is a nice perk when you're trying to fit a lot into a short trip.

On the Disney side, I recently stayed at the JW Marriott Orlando Bonnet Creek Resort & Spa near Disney World and really enjoyed it as well.

For those looking for a more luxe stay, check out the Waldorf Astoria Orlando.

One last tip: Check the Undercover Tourist Crowd Calendar before choosing your dates. It estimates crowd levels at each park on a scale of 1 to 10. When you only have a couple of days, avoiding the busiest dates can make a big difference. I try to aim for a crowd level of 6 or lower.

10. Austin, Texas

One of the best weekend trips in the US for a quirky vibe and Texas barbecue

Austin has always had its own personality, but the city has changed quite a bit over the last several years.

Much of downtown is walkable, the restaurant scene is excellent and varied, Lady Bird Lake is perfect for jogging and paddleboarding, and partying on 6th Street is an...experience.

Across the river, South Congress is a fun area to explore, especially with its mix of old Austin and newer, upscale additions.

You'll find stores like Alo, Kendra Scott, Allbirds, and Outdoor Voices, but walk a little farther down South Congress and you'll get a glimpse of Austin's roots, with longtime favorites like Allen's Boots and vintage clothing shops.

There always seems to be a new hotel and several new restaurants each time I visit. It's hard to keep up with how quickly the city is growing!

And the food scene is one of the best reasons to visit. Once you've had your fill of Texas BBQ, head to Uchi for sushi, Aba for Mediterranean-inspired dishes, The Peacock for cocktails, Jo's Coffee for coffee and tacos, Perla's for seafood, or Launderette for brunch.

Foodies will be spoiled for choice in Austin.

Best hotels in Downtown Austin, TX

  • JW Marriott Austin
  • Four Seasons Hotel Austin
  • Thompson Austin
  • Austin Proper Hotel

If you're looking for something a little more special, Commodore Perry Estate, Auberge Collection is worth a look. Located about 10 minutes north of downtown, this boutique luxury hotel sits on a 10-acre historic estate with gardens, a pool, and an on-site restaurant, Lutie’s. It's a great option for a quieter, more romantic weekend in Austin.

Honorable Mention: New Orleans, Louisiana

I've decided to take New Orleans off my list of the top 10 best weekend getaways in the USA. While the city still has so much to offer, I've found it harder to recommend in recent years.

One of my biggest frustrations has been the cleanliness of the city, particularly in some of the more tourist-heavy areas. Safety has also been a concern, although it's worth mentioning that New Orleans has seen some significant improvements in crime rates since the post-COVID spike.

All in all, New Orleans is still a city worth visiting, especially for its food, history, and music scene. But if you're looking for a weekend getaway with Southern charm, I'd personally choose Charleston over New Orleans.

That said, there's plenty to keep you busy in New Orleans. The food scene alone is a reason to visit. Take your pick from fine dining in historic settings (sometimes haunted!), jazz brunches, modern food halls, farm-to-table restaurants, and global cuisine. This city really is a foodie's paradise.

Spend your days visiting the National WWII Museum (highly recommend!), checking out art galleries, touring the city's famous cemeteries, and wandering through the French Quarter. And, of course, there's Bourbon Street.

Some of our favorite restaurants are Shaya, Luke, La Petite Grocery, Irene's, and Herbsaint. For cocktails, Bar Marilou is a favorite.

Final Thoughts on the Best Weekend Getaways in the USA

I hope this list of the best weekend getaways in the USA has given you a few ideas for your next trip! These are places Jake and I have visited over the years and find ourselves returning to again and again.

One of the things I love about these destinations is that you don't need a full week to enjoy them. Whether you're looking for great restaurants, a little history, time outdoors, or simply a change of scenery, each offers plenty to experience over a long weekend.

Of course, you could easily spend more time exploring many of these cities, but two to three days is enough to get a good feel for what makes each one worth visiting.

    We lived in Charleston, SC for 10+ years and I too struggled with the humanity of the horse + carriage rides when we first arrived. So I made a point to really research the issue. I visited stables while walking around downtown. I talked with people who worked with the animals as well as locals who have witnessed the practice for decades. Here’s what I learned, that was supported by independent research and conversations with large animal veterinarians…

    Draft horses have been used for centuries for manual labor in the farming and logging industries. A well-conditioned draft horses that weighs about 2000 lbs, can very comfortably pull about 8000 – 12,000 lbs. A pair of draft horses can pull up to around 32,000 lbs. The average load of 10 adult passengers is an avg 2000 lbs, well under what these animals were bred to do. These horse are very well taken care of. Each horse only goes out 2-3 per day, max. There are City ordinances in place that prevent carriage rides from occurring when the temperature reaches 95 degrees or the heat index is above 110. This is monitored by the hour and rides will occur at different times of day during cooler temperatures. The horses are well fed, well loved and stables participate in a myriad of public service, educational and community events. One stable used to provide free, horse + carriage rides in our neighborhood free of charge, every Christmas.

    I am a mom. My son grew up in Charleston. We are empathetic, liberal-minded people, much like the majority of the Charleston community. I promise you, I would not ask this of you unless I truly meant it… Please consider removing those comments from your Charleston listing. There is nothing inhumane about the horse + carriage industry in Charleston. You are hurting and villainizing local business owners who love their horses and contribute to the tourism market that fuels the City’s economy.
